title: Subtree

constraints.text: N ≤ 1e5, answers modulo any M ≤ 1e9 (not necessarily prime)

explanation: For every vertex v, count connected black sets containing v. Rerooting: a downward pass for subtrees, an upward pass for 'everything outside', using prefix/suffix products because M may not be prime.
traps: You can't divide by (down[c] + 1) to exclude a child: M isn't prime and the value may be 0 mod M.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: down[v] = # connected black sets inside v's subtree that contain v; up[v] = the same for the part outside v's subtree, hanging from v's parent
dp[v] = # connected black sets in v's subtree containing v, recomputed with every vertex as root
options.why: Right DP, but N roots × O(N) = 1e10.

options.text: dp[mask] = whether black set mask is connected
dp[v][c] = colourings of v's subtree with v coloured c
options.why: That's Independent Set's state; this problem needs connectivity to v.

extraLayers.explanation: 'Answer for every root' is the rerooting signal: one DP for inside the subtree, one for outside.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: down[v] = Π (down[c] + 1); ans[v] = down[v] · (up[v] + 1); up[c] = (up[v] + 1) · Π over siblings s ≠ c of (down[s] + 1) via prefix/suffix products

options.why: Division is unsafe: M isn't prime.
Choices in different child subtrees multiply.
Same answer for every vertex — ignores the 'must contain v' part.

extraLayers.explanation: Each child is either cut off (1) or connected (down[c] ways); the outside part works the same way through the parent.
